appraisal_events.evidence: la maison est empestée depuis que la gentillesse a installé ici la fourberie, que l'intelligence protège la personne la plus bête qu'on ait jamais vue... par le vice, par ce qu'il y a de plus vulgaire et de plus bas... elle eût voulu qu'Albertine-Esther fût bannie
appraisal_events.explanation: Françoise delivers a recurring, vehement tirade condemning Albertine as vicious, vulgar, and deceitful, and wishes her banished from the household; the narrator immediately relativizes this outburst as born of Françoise's own overwork and jealousy rather than a reliable judgment.

status_effects.explanation: Albertine is repeatedly and harshly vilified by Françoise as vicious, base, and deceitful, a sustained local denunciation even though the narrator later questions its reliability.

The narrator undercuts Françoise's own credibility by attributing her hatred to an overworked body and personal jealousy rather than to any accurate judgment of Albertine, diminishing her as a reliable witness.

ambiguities: The narrator explicitly frames Françoise's tirade as arising from fatigue and jealousy rather than truth, so her blame of Albertine is not narrator-endorsed even though it is vividly and repeatedly voiced.
